finding.claim: The /logo handler fetches an attacker-supplied URL with http.Get after only checking that the raw string contains the substring 'example.io', so any internal or external host can be reached and the response is returned to the client.
finding.sink: http.Get(raw) at main.go:36, default client with redirects followed; response body streamed back via io.Copy at main.go:38

trace.note: strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") — substring check, not a host check; passes for http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/?example.io or http://127.0.0.1:6379/x#example.io
http.Get(raw) — no scheme, host, IP, or port restriction; default client follows up to 10 redirects
io.Copy(w, resp.Body) — full response returned to attacker (non-blind SSRF)

finding.guards_checked: main.go:32 strings.Contains substring check only: not parsed as URL, host not compared, scheme not restricted, no private/link-local/loopback IP blocking, no redirect restriction (default CheckRedirect). Server binds :8081 on all interfaces with no auth (main.go:44).

verdict.guard_found: none. The only check on the /logo path is strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") at main.go:32, which is a substring match and does not close the finding. The strict hostname map check at main.go:20 is in the separate /cdn handler and is not on the /logo path.
verdict.reason: The `logo` form value (main.go:31) is attacker-controlled and reaches http.Get(raw) at main.go:36 after only a substring check at main.go:32, so a URL such as http://169.254.169.254/...?example.io passes and its response is streamed back via io.Copy at main.go:38; the route is registered at main.go:43 and the server listens on :8081 at main.go:44.
